Meeting header: 2026-12-30 15:00 PST | Duration: 52 mins | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Marcus Holt (Redwood) -- Alex Kim, Samir Patel, Dana Ortiz, Luis Mendoza (OrionGrid)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy holidays if you're still in holi--, um, appreciate you carving time. quick round of intros?
[00:15] Alex: yeah thanks jordan, alex here, head of partnerships at OrionGrid, we run the marketplace program and partner integrations.
[00:22] Samir: samir, director cloud eng, focus on our GPU infra and multi-tenant offerings.
[00:28] Dana: dana ortiz, ciso, i'll be looking at compliance and key mgmt.
[00:33] Luis: luis, solutions eng, i'll be the main technical contact for integrations.
[00:38] Jordan: great -- i'm jordan, AE, priya is our se, and marcus runs partnerships for redwood. priya do you wanna quick summarize what we do?
[00:46] Priya: sure, quick high level -- redwood provides a unified inference platform, hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and a private deployment option. we do model cataloging, autoscaling for dedicated pools, kv caching and prefix caching, and built-in routing policies for latency vs cost. we also have a partner marketplace flow for third-party infra vendors.
[01:10] Samir: ok sounds good. our primary interest is twofold: 1) list a marketplace offering where our customers can spin up redwood-backed endpoints on our infra, and 2) a private deployment/managed offering where we provision dedicated gpus for large customers but use redwood's runtime.
[01:28] Jordan: perfect, that's in our sweet spot. a couple clarifying q's -- what does your infra look like today? what gpu types, ork, and network patterns?
[01:36] Samir: we're mostly ampere-class -- a mixture of A100S and next-gen X2 in some racks, we run k8s clusters with nvidia device plugins and a custom provisioning layer, customers can choose pinned nodes. network wise we offer VPC peering, private endpoints, and marketplace provisioning.
[01:52] Priya: good -- those GPUs are compatible with our runtime, we do per-kernel selection and quantization-aware paths. is there a preference for dedicated vs shared?
[02:03] Samir: for marketplace we want a self-serve mode that spins up ephemeral capacity; for enterprise customers we'd do dedicated pools. the tricky bit is multi-tenant isolation and billing reconciliation.
[02:14] Marcus: billing is solvable -- we support usage-based invoicing plus partner revenue share. we'll share the partner economics doc.
[02:21] Alex: also curious on how the private deployment works -- do you ship a control plane into a partner VPC or do you run control plane in redwood and only data plane in partner infra?
[02:33] Priya: we do both models. for fully managed private deployments we can run a private control plane in your cloud region (customer-managed networking) or an on-prem package if needed. in the marketplace / self-serve case we typically run control plane and route calls to partner-hosted data plane nodes.
[02:51] Dana: from a security standpoint we need to understand KMS integration, audit logs, and whether we can force keys to HSM if required. also SSO and provisioning via SAML.
[03:05] Jordan: totally -- we already have KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google KMS, and customer-HSM via bring-your-own). audit logs and per-request tracing are available in the console. we can provide SOC2 and ISO docs.
[03:20] Dana: ok please send those, and a questionnaire -- we'll want to review before any pilot.
[03:25] Jordan: will do.
[03:28] Luis: on the tech side, latency numbers -- what's your typical token latency on a 2k context with A100 equivalent?
[03:36] Priya: it depends on model and quantization. for a 2k context using a 7B-ish model optimized on A100 we see p95 token latency around 60-90ms depending on batching; for LLMs with KV cache warm we can do lower. if you want higher qps we'll propose batching and dedicated pools.
[03:54] Samir: ok we expect bursty workloads from inference products and steady throughput for fine-tuning inference. can redwood support autoscaling of dedicated pools and graceful degrade back to smaller models?
[04:07] Priya: yes autoscaling policies and fallback to cheaper variants is built into our routing. you can define policies by latency, cost, or region.
[04:15] Alex: interesting. on the marketplace side -- what's required to list an offering? container image? helm chart?
[04:23] Marcus: our partner marketplace flow supports a few options: 1) we provide a pre-built image (we can vendor your runtime as an image), 2) a helm chart to deploy into your k8s, or 3) a managed data-plane where we provision nodes and you provide capacity. most partners prefer the image + marketplace provisioning.
[04:40] Luis: do you support hardware scheduling to pins specific gpus per request? and how is GPU passthrough handled?
[04:46] Priya: we integrate with the device plugin and have scheduling hints; for dedicated pools we can pin instances. passthrough details depend on your vm/driver stack but we've worked with partners on SR-IOV and vnode setups. sometimes transcripts of customer's config are messy so we'll validate in the SE deep-dive.
[05:05] Samir: good. are there limitations around model sizes or kv caching across restarts? we do some long-context use-cases.
[05:13] Priya: we support KV cache persistence across warm restarts in dedicated pools; for ephemeral marketplace instances cache warm-up is required. very large-context models require attention to memory/host binding; we'll need your expected seq lengths.
[05:29] Alex: from a go-to-market angle, we want co-branded collateral and a listing page. what kind of partner enablement do you provide?
[05:38] Marcus: partner playbooks, sales enablement, onboarding workshops, technical integration docs, and joint webinars. we can also provide a sandbox account for your sales engineers.
[05:47] Dana: another security note -- can you enforce tenant-level encryption where our customers' model weights are encrypted with their key, and can you prove key separation?
[05:56] Priya: we support per-customer keying for model artifacts and data at rest; key separation is done via customer-KMS or your HSM. we can show the architecture and certs in security docs.
[06:10] Jordan: okay, high level sounds aligned. let's talk pilot scope and timeline -- what would a minimum viable pilot look like?
[06:18] Alex: maybe a marketplace listing + one enterprise customer trial where we provision a dedicated pool for 3 months; we want to validate onboarding, RBAC, and billing.
[06:28] Jordan: that seems reasonable. sample pilot plan -- week 0 sign MSA/NDA, week 1-2 security review and SE deep-dive, week 3 implement marketplace listing or private control plane, week 4 onboard first customer and run benchmarks.
[06:44] Samir: timeline wise we have a few customers ready to test in Jan. can we get an SE deep-dive next week?
[06:51] Priya: yes i'll schedule a 90-minute slot with luis and samir for the week of jan 4.
[06:58] Luis: perfect. also we'll need a contract appendix for partner revenue share.
[07:03] Marcus: noted, i'll share a draft partner revenue appendix and listing terms.
[07:09] Dana: one more item -- audit logging retention. some customers need 7 years retention for audit trails; can you support extended retention or do we have to export logs?
[07:20] Jordan: we offer configurable retention on logs; long-term retention is an add-on and we can ship logs to your S3/archive or maintain them on our console depending on the plan.
[07:31] Alex: ok good. any technical red flags so far?
[07:34] Samir: mostly details -- we need to validate kernel compatibility with our firmware, and the marketplace onboarding automation.
[07:42] Priya: we'll include a compatibility checklist. sometimes the transcription of ops configs is messy -- we'll collect exact driver/kernel versions in the SE call.
[07:51] Jordan: all right let's recap next steps: send partner packet, security docs, schedule SE deep-dive, and Marcus will share revenue appendix.
[07:59] Alex: agreed.
[08:02] Jordan: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
